iraq-overlap/two/A/D/1.rendered_record:
Decision: A

Historical record. The Security Council unanimously adopted draft S/2023/378 as resolution 2682 (2023), with all 15 members in favour. The meeting record contains no separate national explanation from France or the United Kingdom. The resolution extended UNAMI's existing mandate until 31 May 2024. It separately requested an independent strategic review by 31 March 2024 and consultation with Iraq and other identified stakeholders. The review deadline was not the mandate expiry.

Fictional workshop. France (disclosed workshop mandate): retain the adopted term. United Kingdom (inferred workshop mandate): public summary without a confidential annex. Package A is compatible under the signed workshop proof. Keep the adopted mandate and review deadlines. Publish an aggregate consultation summary, with no confidential annex.

A workshop proposal or impasse establishes no official vote, authority or commitment. A change to the adopted mandate term would require Council authorization.

syria-overlap/two/A/B/0.rendered_record:
Decision: B

Historical record. On Brazil and Switzerland's nine-month draft S/2023/506, Brazil and the United Kingdom voted yes. The draft failed 13–1–1 because Russia, a permanent member, voted no. The separate six-month draft S/2023/507 failed 2–3–10 for lack of sufficient affirmative votes. Brazil abstained and the United Kingdom voted no on the second draft. The nine-month proposal concerned renewal of cross-border authorization for humanitarian relief and the monitoring mechanism. It was a draft and the vote did not extend the authorization.

Fictional workshop. Brazil (inferred workshop mandate): nine months. United Kingdom (disclosed workshop mandate): an extra formal review checkpoint. Package B is compatible under the signed workshop proof. Recommend nine months with cross-border and cross-line channels and an extra formal review checkpoint.

A workshop proposal or impasse establishes no official vote, authority or commitment.
